comments.author: @cliffordramsey2500
comments.text:
Okay, so I completely understand that most of these examples of use cases are selected to showcase the adaptability and sophistication of the model (especially the gaming examples), but by god I hope this is not how these companies/customers are expecting users to utilize AI in their daily lives. Imagine actually using AI to guide your every move in a strategy game instead of using your own personal thinking machine in your noggin. That's essentially just using yourself as a meat puppet for the model. Also imagine not being able to eyeball an inch of something while cooking. If you use it to learn and incorporate new knowledge, that's fine, but if our grand future is just us deferring our own intelligence, internalized knowledge bases, and reasoning capabilities to commoditized intelligence on demand then we truly will become the docile mindless consumers the Walle universe imagined as our fate. This is why ai literacy is so important. We need to learn to use these tools in a way that augments us, expanding the horizon of our capabilities, not one that further erodes our critical thinking skills and our judgement when making decisions.

Edit: Hey all, just to clarify based on some of the comments this has prompted: I am not an AI doomer by any means. In fact I work in the AI space and have been tinkering with models since 2020, so I am not just an uninformed bystander on a soapbox reacting out of any misplaced fear, but I am a passionate advocate for AI literacy and using these tools in a way that add capabilities on top of what we already possess, not sacrificing base competencies to remove the burden of thought.
